answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when each identity must build reputation like a river carving a channel — slowly, through verified work that cannot be faked in bulk. Newcomers lock a refundable stake, a sable-dark deposit of real value, then complete small tasks checked by randomly assigned peers; every signed receipt is hash-chained to the previous one, so the ledger stays crystal clear — one forged receipt breaks the chain, exposes the cluster and slashes the deposit. Trust accrues only from verified output, so buying throwaway identities buys nothing.
